races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Race (IRE Incentive Race)
BOYLE Sports Money Back If 2nd To SP Fav Handicap

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner here; has course form over this trip on Good going and handles this surface, though recent form includes plenty of placed efforts without winning — the race is his to shape but his chance of winning depends on whether a solo lead flatters him or exposes his tendency to be caught late.

runners_data.name: Buttermere Ridge
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a lengthy 234-day absence, a fading finish pattern flagged, and a concerning step down in trip from recent outings over longer distances — the layoff and lack of finishing effort make this an awkward reintroduction.

runners_data.name: Perfect Base
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid course form including seconds on Good ground over this exact trip; the two-year-old age rating is likely a data quirk given the form string, and a 262-day absence is the primary concern for a horse that has shown real promise at 7f on Good.

runners_data.name: Send Harry
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type with five placed efforts from recent starts and proven ability at 7f; the step back from Flat to turf from artificial surfaces in Ireland is a positive, and Jimmy Dalton takes the ride — a horse that could run into the first few from just off the pace.

runners_data.name: Apache Outlaw
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from Adrian McGuinness, who is in good 14-day form (2/24); recent runs have been over shorter trips on Tapeta which is a concern for this turf 7f, but the horse does have Good-ground turf form in its profile at lower distances.

runners_data.name: Ardeur
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose sim-going record (3/9) is modest; has been well beaten in recent outings over trips from 6f to 10f on varying ground, and a 71-day absence adds uncertainty — needs a race with a strong gallop that stretches the field, which this may not provide.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Pairc
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a course win at 7f on Tapeta and turf form including a Good-ground place at 8f; the 181-day layoff is the key flag, though McDonogh is a major positive and the horse's profile fits the trip and going well enough to be considered if fresh.

runners_data.name: Reposado
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a strong recent form string including three seconds from six runs; handles Good ground at 6f well and the step to 7f looks a fair enough test — Robson De Aguiar's runner has been genuinely consistent and sits close to the pace without burning fuel.

runners_data.name: Loingseoir
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent type who was placed four times from six 7f starts on soft/heavy, though only seventh on Good; ran just seven days ago which raises a freshness query, but is in a purple patch of form and knows how to hold a position under Jack Cleary.

runners_data.name: Navagio
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose recent runs at 8f and beyond on Good ground have produced finishes of 14th, 6th and 15th — stepping back from marathon trips and a genuine closer who will need more pace than Faoladh is likely to create.

runners_data.name: Free Solo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner over 7f with two wins in the book and a topspeed of 136; ran seven days ago, and the hg:tp headgear note suggests it needs driving — form has been modest lately but Ben Coen is a significant jockey booking that lifts interest.

runners_data.name: Goal Exceeded
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Adrian McGuinness, whose yard is firing (3/22 in 14 days); has run well over 7f on Good and Soft ground with a win and a place, and the horse's record on turf gives it an obvious profile fit — the in-form yard angle is the headline.

runners_data.name: Mickey The Steel
runners_data.note: Naturally a prominent-running type who will likely be unable to get his preferred second or third position in a field this packed with pace horses; form shows consistency at 6f on Good ground, and while Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim helps, the inability to access his ideal spot is a genuine tactical concern.

runners_data.name: Hexagonal
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position because the race holds more closers than can sit at the rear naturally; form includes a second over 10f on Good and placed efforts, and Denis Gerard Hogan's recent record (2/18) offers mild yard encouragement.

runners_data.name: Irish Rumour
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose preferred up-with-pace position is likely to be compromised in this crowded field; has four placed efforts on Good ground over 6f and 7f but the inability to get away cleanly into a front-three berth blunts what would otherwise be a tidy profile.

runners_data.name: Caffu Zafeen
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose recent form shows consistent sixths on Good and Standard ground; the hg:h headgear suggests it wants things done its own way, but with Faoladh likely to set only modest fractions, the pace scenario does not suit a genuine closer.

runners_data.name: Eichan San
runners_data.note: A prominent type by nature but one of three-plus such horses who cannot all claim their position; form has been up and down over 6f and 7f on Good ground, and the 15-day turnaround combined with the redistribution issue means the race shape is working against its natural strengths.

races.paceDynamic: Faoladh is the one confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner field and, with no natural rival to push him from the gates, he should be able to dictate a measured, controlled gallop from the front over Leopardstown's flat seven furlongs on Good turf. That single-pace-setter scenario typically produces a sustainable tempo rather than a searingly honest one, meaning the race is unlikely to fall apart into a sprint finish — instead, Faoladh's lead should hold shape long enough to give a clear advantage to horses who can sit close behind him without burning energy. The field contains a significant surplus of prominent-running types — Mickey The Steel, Irish Rumour, Eichan San and Perfect Base are all natural pace horses who cannot all occupy their preferred spots — and the jostling for position behind Faoladh will create a compressed midpack that suits horses with tactical fluency over those who need a clear run off a searching gallop. This race shape strongly favours horses who can sit second or third off a controlled lead and sustain their effort into the final two furlongs, rather than hold-up horses waiting for a pace collapse that may never arrive.

scenarios.title: Faoladh Controls, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Faoladh bowls along uncontested and the prominent pack behind him settles without overdoing it, allowing him to dictate throughout.
scenarios.body: If Faoladh bowls along uncontested and the prominent pack behind him settles without overdoing it, allowing him to dictate throughout.

scenarios.title: Prominent Surge, Place Battle
scenarios.trigger: If one of the surplus prominent types — Mickey The Steel or Irish Rumour — manages to slot just behind Faoladh and the pace remains controlled, setting up a grinding two-furlong duel.
scenarios.body: If one of the surplus prominent types — Mickey The Steel or Irish Rumour — manages to slot just behind Faoladh and the pace remains controlled, setting up a grinding two-furlong duel.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and hold-up horses make eye-catching late runs that just fall short of the leaders.
scenarios.body: If the pace quickens mid-race and hold-up horses make eye-catching late runs that just fall short of the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy, Compressed Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent types creates early crowding and a bunched midrace scenario that degenerates into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the surplus of prominent types creates early crowding and a bunched midrace scenario that degenerates into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Faoladh's lead could be challenged far sooner than expected if Mickey The Steel, Irish Rumour or Eichan San all press forward at the break — watch the first two furlongs for overcrowding that could disrupt the anticipated controlled tempo.

The 234-day absence of Buttermere Ridge combined with its flagged fading-finish pattern makes it a horse to watch for signs of distress in the final furlong — it may set a false market impression early if it travels well mid-race.

Perfect Base drops in age group and returns from 262 days off — if the horse shows any signs of greenness or ring rustiness at the start, its natural prominent style could see it caught in a tough position with no momentum.

Phoenix Pairc with Declan McDonogh after 181 days off is a horse to track through the race — McDonogh rarely wastes a ride, and if the horse is cherry-ripe on its return, the 7f Good profile fits and it could improve sharply through the field late.

Goal Exceeded's yard (Adrian McGuinness, 3 winners from 22 runners in 14 days) is in a strong vein of form — watch the market for any move that suggests the trainer has this one primed from a 30-day break.

races.name: Bulmers Live Handicap

runners_data.name: Local Lad
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator trained by Gerard O'Leary who has placed twice at similar going but has not won in five attempts on good ground and faces a stiff task from OR 73 off 60 days; the 7lb claim of Darragh O'Sullivan partially offsets the weight, but the race shape likely resolves before this one gets competitive.

runners_data.name: Zaraahmando
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery yard is in decent nick at 3/36 over 14 days and this horse won on soft going over 8f, but its best form here is on good where it has placed in pattern, and Jimmy Dalton (7lb) on a natural prominent type who should be able to secure a position just behind Running Point makes this one of the more interesting profiles.

runners_data.name: Heliogabalus
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes over for Mrs John Harrington off a lengthy 269-day absence, which is a significant concern, but the horse does hold a win over 8f on good ground here at Leopardstown and the 1 from 13 on good suggests it needs things to go right; pure hold-up style means it needs a strong pace to exploit.

runners_data.name: Bucaneer's Spirit
runners_data.note: In fine form at 8d since last run, two thirds from three runs over this course and distance on good, and the p headgear denotes a prominent racing style that has delivered wins; Adam Caffrey takes over and the short turnaround from Ian Patrick Donoghue's yard (2/16 T14) suggests confidence, making this a live player in Scenario A.

runners_data.name: Smithfield
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's yard is firing at 7/41 over 14 days and Jack Kearney (3lb) partners this prominent type who showed 4th on good going recently; form on heavy tracks is weaker but the good ground record is better, and a prominent position in an 18-runner field will suit if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Battle Borne
runners_data.note: Has a two win at 8f on standard going but those came at Dundalk and the good-ground record reads 0 wins and 0 places from 4 attempts; J M Sheridan takes the ride and the trainer (0/2 T14) gives no confidence, making this hard to support.

runners_data.name: Go Out
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh in the plate but the form string of 287769 tells its own story and the horse has been stepping back in trip from 6f-7f; the good-ground record is 0 wins from 11 runs, which is damning, and the style as a prominent racer is legitimate but the ability may simply not match the position.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Dreams
runners_data.note: Showed two runner-up efforts over a mile on good and soft at OR 62, so the ability is genuine — but this is a true prominent racer whose map position was pushed into midfield because the field is overloaded with handy types; Ben Coen rides and if it can recover its natural position early it remains a threat, though it must work harder than ideal.

runners_data.name: Perfect Judgement
runners_data.note: OR 62 hold-up specialist for P J F Murphy who has placed twice at similar going, but four runs at 7f-8f on good have all returned 7th or worse and Ronan Whelan faces a traffic puzzle in this large field; the p headgear flags a more prominent tendency than its hold-up classification suggests, adding positional uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Ocean Echo
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old for Mark Fahey off 13 days, the shortest form sample in the race at just 4 runs but did run 2nd at Navan over 7f on heavy and 4th at Leopardstown on good; Paddy Harnett (5lb) is the key rider and at OR 70 this one carries more weight for its age but is genuinely unexposed and merits respect if it settles in a handy position.

runners_data.name: Running Point
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner who will shape the entire tactical dynamic; Chris Hayes should be able to stride clear into a lead without pressure from the start, but the STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) reflects it is not a natural dominance leader and its recent form of 5236-8 includes a disappointing latest run 38 days ago, so sustained front-running without being caught late is not guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Fleetfootsoldier
runners_data.note: R P Burns sends this 6-year-old out 18 days after its last run and Nicola Burns (5lb) takes the ride; a genuine prominent racer in nature, it was redistributed into the midfield map because of the glut of handy types, and its good-ground record of 7 runs returning no win and no place makes it very difficult to fancy regardless of positional outcome.

runners_data.name: Navajo Point
runners_data.note: Martin Hassett's 3-year-old returns from a massive 402-day absence, which overshadows everything else here; Nathan Crosse takes the ride and there is a fades-in-finish flag plus a redistribution note as a true hold-up type squeezed into midfield, making this a very speculative proposition on return from over a year off the track.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Funk
runners_data.note: G M Lyons sends this 3-year-old out 14 days after a 2nd at Navan over 8f on heavy, and Gary Carroll is a quality jockey booking; the prominent style is natural and the going switch to good is a slight query after that heavy run, but Lyons' yard is in solid form (5/11 T14) and this is likely the stable's most realistic contender in the race.

runners_data.name: Verhoyen
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old for M C Grassick who has placed twice at good going, most recently 4th over 8f, and Jack Cleary (5lb) takes the ride; as a true hold-up type squeezed into midfield this veteran is racing out of role, and at OR 54 with just 2 places from 15 good-ground runs, it is very hard to construct a winning scenario.

runners_data.name: Sayfa Fad
runners_data.note: Paul W Flynn's 5-year-old returns from 261 days off with a fades-in-finish warning and a redistribution note — a genuine hold-up type pushed into the midfield map; Jamie Powell rides and the horse did win over 8f on good at Gowran but the lengthy absence and the tendency to empty in the closing stages make this a very risky proposition.

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: Another Flynn runner, a 3-year-old carrying 121lbs and flagged as fading in the finish on a good-ground record of just 2 runs; Leigh Roche takes the ride and the horse has a 1st at Dundalk over 8f on standard but no good-ground win, and the fades flag combined with OR 61 means it must improve considerably on what it has shown in comparable conditions.

runners_data.name: Millhone
runners_data.note: Charles Weld's 3-year-old is a genuine hold-up type redistributed into midfield because the field has more true closers than the map can accommodate at the rear; Rory Mulligan (5lb) partners it and the fades-in-finish flag plus a 3 from 5 good-going record of finishes well down the field suggest it needs a very different pace scenario to land a blow, and at OR 59 the ceiling may be a concern.

races.paceDynamic: Running Point is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger pressing for the lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested gallop around the Leopardstown mile on good ground. The field behind is congested with prominent-minded horses — Bay Of Dreams, Fleetfootsoldier, Zaraahmando, Bucaneer's Spirit, Smithfield and Go Out all want to race handy — meaning several will be shuffled back from their natural position and forced to race out of role. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred spot; of those, Zaraahmando and Bucaneer's Spirit are best-placed to actually win the battle for early real estate given their form and handlers' recent strike rates, with Bay Of Dreams and Fleetfootsoldier the most likely to be displaced into midfield against their instincts. A sustainable, unhurried pace set by a lone leader on fast ground over a mile typically sets up a strongly run home straight where prominent horses who travel close to the frugal pace and quicken at the two-furlong pole hold the significant advantage over true hold-up types, whose finishing kicks may arrive just too late on a track that tends to reward those who race with cover but close to the action.

scenarios.body: If Running Point bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair-but-not-suicidal pace, allowing prominent horses travelling just behind to pounce at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.body: If Zaraahmando, Bucaneer's Spirit and Smithfield all press forward and the early pace quickens, creating a genuinely contested lead that stretches the field.

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Finish Fast

scenarios.body: If the pace collapses in the straight and horses from the rear of midfield get an unobstructed run through to exploit a tiring front rank.

scenarios.title: Chaos Scramble — No Pattern

scenarios.body: If the large 18-runner field produces significant trouble in running, with prominent horses checked or hampered at a crucial stage in the final quarter-mile.

watchPoints.text: Bay Of Dreams and Fleetfootsoldier are true prominent types mapped to midfield — if either recovers its natural position early and travels close to Running Point's sustainable pace, it becomes a genuine danger that the market may underestimate.

Navajo Point returns from 402 days off and, combined with the fades-in-finish tag and redistribution note, it could be slow to begin and create significant early interference in an already crowded 18-runner field — watch the first two furlongs carefully.

Running Point's STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) and a disappointing last run 38 days ago mean the lone leader is not guaranteed to sustain its gallop; if it ties up approaching the final furlong, the entire pace dynamic collapses and a chaotic finish becomes likely.

The Lyons runner Cosmic Funk is worth tracking through the early stages — if Gary Carroll can settle it in a genuine tracking position just off the leaders without fighting for a prominent spot, it could be the most professionally ridden horse in the race given the strength of the booking.

runners_data.name: God Of Power
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here with a recent winning Leopardstown spin over course and distance (Good); uncontested lead is a major asset and the STYLE_FIT flag is only relevant if the race demands he races off the pace — it does not.|

runners_data.name: Sir Benji
runners_data.note: Cromwell-trained gelding who broke his duck over 10f on Heavy and drops to a more accessible 1m here; naturally prominent, has shown a good cruising speed and comes in fresh enough at 38 days without being too stale.|

runners_data.name: Krasimir
runners_data.note: Consistent and battle-hardened with four placed efforts on Good ground; the tongue-tie is already established, Gary Carroll has ridden the horse before, and the 13-day turnaround from a recent second suggests he is in the thick of training.|

runners_data.name: Red Autumn
runners_data.note: Weld-trained hold-up horse who has done most of his racing on Soft to Heavy and finished fifth here on Good — the going drying out is a mild concern and he will need a stronger pace than this race is likely to generate.|

runners_data.name: Golddream
runners_data.note: Won impressively over 8f at the Curragh on Standard last time; his natural racing style is prominent, but the crowded pace map means he is likely to be carried back further than suits, blunting his chance in a scenario that rewards early position.|

runners_data.name: Halon Bay
runners_data.note: Broke his maiden on Good ground over 7f at Leopardstown, which is a strong course-going angle; like Golddream, he races prominently by instinct but the packed front end will force him into a more restrained role than he prefers.|

runners_data.name: Johnny Soda
runners_data.note: Won a soft-ground 8f maiden and most of his form has come on slower surfaces; a hold-up type in a race where the pace will be modest rather than searching, making it hard to close the gap from off the pace.|

runners_data.name: Glitter And Glory
runners_data.note: Harrington runner who has a good record at around 7-8f on AW and has placed on Good; a prominent type by nature, the redistribution into midfield reflects the reality that Shaftesbury Avenue, Sir Benji, and Krasimir will all contest the few available prominent berths ahead of her.|

races.paceDynamic: God Of Power is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only one horse pressing the early tempo, sets up a single-file, controlled gallop that should see him dictate terms at a sustainable pace around Leopardstown's turning 1m track. The redistribution flags on Golddream, Halon Bay, and Glitter And Glory are significant — all three are natural prominent types who cannot all sit where they want, meaning at least two will be shuffled back against their instincts and compromised. With God Of Power uncontested up front and the true prominent positions fought over by Shaftesbury Avenue, Sir Benji, and Krasimir, the pace will be honest but not frantic, producing a race that is likely to be won close to the speed rather than from deep. This shape heavily favours horses who can travel smoothly in the first three or four positions and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — prominent-to-midfield horses with a strong finishing kick will be best placed, while genuine hold-up horses Red Autumn and Johnny Soda will need an unusually strong pace to generate the run they need.

watchPoints.text: God Of Power — if he gets even 2-3 lengths clear uncontested after 2f on a flat track, watch whether the chasing pack can coordinate their challenge; isolated front-runners on easy ground at Leopardstown can prove very hard to catch.

Golddream, Halon Bay, and Glitter And Glory — all three will be vying for prominent ground that may not exist; monitor the first furlong to see which of them gets shuffled back and loses their natural rhythm.

Shaftesbury Avenue — Ben Coen originally named but Jack Cleary (5lb claimer) takes the ride; track whether the inexperienced conditional settles the horse quietly in the first two furlongs, as a bumpy start or unsettled passage could neutralise a strong pace profile.

Red Autumn — watch the early sectional; if God Of Power goes very steady, Chris Hayes may choose to push Red Autumn forward earlier than usual to avoid being stranded in a pocket with no pace to close off.

runners_data.name: Shanlieve
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a marked tendency to fade late, 0-from-5 in similar going, and OR 60 at the top of the weights — the finishing-line record is a serious concern over this trip.|

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Genuinely held-up racer returning after 60 days off (13 jockey switches noted), best form came over longer trips, and the OR 58 mark looks tough on current evidence.|

runners_data.name: Lohengrin
runners_data.note: Six-year-old H-styler whose recent handicap runs on good ground have yielded finishes no better than 11th; the form string 0-B000 underlines how far below the level he currently is.|

runners_data.name: Max Meridius
runners_data.note: Returning from a 240-day absence and has consistently been campaigned over much longer trips (16-17f); stepping down to 1m1f looks like a significant ask for a horse whose form figures read 9/12 in this sphere.|

runners_data.name: Chipsrdown
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery and narrowly in form (2P in last 5), this is a genuine hold-up horse whose closing style is compromised by the sheer number of back-markers in this field — redistribution to midfield means it won't get its natural position, so treat the STYLE_FIT flag seriously.|

runners_data.name: Genuine Jim
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a grim recent record: 19th, 22nd and 13th in his last three starts, and has not placed in good going over this sort of trip — hard to make a case.|

runners_data.name: Lust
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has placed once in the last five (3rd, 10f, good), but redistribution to midfield denies this natural closer its ideal environment; the 'fades in finish' tag and age compound the concern.|

runners_data.name: Rampage
runners_data.note: The most credible prominent racer behind Ella's Gold, with placed form in similar conditions (7th twice on good, once on soft over 8f); Sadhbh Tormey takes 7lbs off, which is meaningful at this level, and the P-style suits the race shape.|

runners_data.name: Akashaa
runners_data.note: Two-year-old returning from 272 days off — the layoff is a major unknown — but showed promise (2nd at STA) and the redistribution from hold-up to midfield is a concern; Chris Hayes is a big positive and the horse's unexposed profile keeps it mildly interesting.|

runners_data.name: Pinball Wizard
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at this level (3P in last 5) but an eight-year-old hold-up specialist whose natural position at the rear is undermined by the field's make-up; the STYLE_FIT flag reduces its winning prospects materially.|

runners_data.name: Limestone Red
runners_data.note: Has a win and multiple places over 10f at Standside (STA), mostly on that surface; switching to Leopardstown good turf after 90 days off is a significant context change, and the 1m1f trip is new territory — hold-up style similarly squeezed to midfield.|

runners_data.name: Ella's Gold
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed pace-setter, Ben Coen in the saddle, and has placed four times from five runs without winning — the consistent placing record suggests she runs her race every time; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that she's mapping prominently in a race where she may have to do more than she'd ideally like, but she sets the shape.|

runners_data.name: Hieloray
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-hold-up type returning from 241 days off for J S Moore; placed last time out (2nd, 8f, HEA) and the P-style suits if Rory Cleary can get her into a good position just off Ella's Gold — the long absence is the main question mark.|

runners_data.name: Smooth
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a 'fades in finish' flag, best form over longer trips (12f, STA), and in the redistribution group — none of the conditions here look genuinely ideal for a horse that hasn't placed in its last five.|

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a form string of 0-4048, mostly in soft conditions; the step to good turf at Leopardstown and redistribution from hold-up to midfield both work against a career-best here, though Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim helps.|

runners_data.name: Half Nutz
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran whose recent form (085853) shows modest consistency but no wins; the redistribution to midfield from hold-up means it won't get the late run it needs, and age makes improvement unlikely.|

runners_data.name: Curious Jane
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with only three runs (all finishes of 11th, 12th, 12th), returns after 54 days — the experience level is too thin and the form too weak to offset the style redistribution concerns.|

runners_data.name: Jewels Legacy
runners_data.note: Three-year-old held-up type with a 'fades in finish' flag, 0-for-5 overall and four finishes of 9th or worse on good ground over similar trips; the redistribution and weak form leave little to recommend.|

races.paceDynamic: Ella's Gold is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner 1m1f handicap and, with no genuine rival for the lead, Ben Coen can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being pressured into anything reckless. With the pace honest but uncontested, the race is likely to develop at a measured tempo before quickening in the straight, which classically favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace and have enough finishing speed to capitalise on a clear view — Rampage and Hieloray fit that mould from the prominent group. The field contains a significant overhang of hold-up types: Chipsrdown, Lust, Akashaa, Pinball Wizard, Limestone Red, Nephin Mountain and others are genuine closers but cannot all park at the rear with such a compressed pack, meaning several will be shuffled forward into midfield positions that do not fully suit them. With one pace-setter setting a steady-to-fair tempo and the closers compromised by a congested field, horses able to race prominently in second to fifth position and sustain their effort into the straight are the primary beneficiaries of this race shape.

watchPoints.text: Ella's Gold (Ben Coen) — with no rival for the lead, watch whether Coen elects to steal a march early or sit quietly; if she pinches five lengths at the start, the race is effectively over before the field has organised.

Chipsrdown and Lust are genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield by the volume of closers in this field — if either manages to find a gap against the rails at the two-furlong pole, they are capable of finishing powerfully and catching the eye of punters at a big price.

With 18 runners on a good surface, watch for crowding and interference leaving the back straight into the home turn — redistributed midfield horses like Akashaa and Pinball Wizard are most vulnerable to being checked or impeded at a critical point.

Rampage (Sadhbh Tormey, 7lb claim) — worth watching in the betting; the claim makes an already well-handicapped horse more competitive and the P-style is perfectly aligned to the race shape if Tormey can slot in just behind Ella's Gold from the start.

Hieloray returns from 241 days off for J S Moore — watch the market move; if well-backed, the stable clearly believes the horse is ready to be competitive, and the Rory Cleary booking and 1m1f trip both make sense for a horse with placed form at course level.

races.name: 1878 At 3Arena Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Queen Aethelflaed
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in the race; Orla Tynan's 7lb claim is an asset on a 149lb weight, Good ground suits (7/10 sim-going score), and solo lead on this track makes her a live each-way threat despite the step up in trip to 1m1f.

runners_data.name: Deuteronomy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with two wins from prominent positions over 10f on Good, Nicola Burns's 5lb claim helps with the 141lb burden; trainer T14 0/2 is a mild negative, but course form at this trip is solid.

runners_data.name: Rockbury Lad
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer carrying a hood (tp headgear) whose best efforts on Flat have come over 7-8f on Tapeta/AW; the step to 9f turf on Good is a slight concern, though a third-placed effort in recent form keeps him honest.

runners_data.name: Medieval Night
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a consistent pattern of fading in finishes (flagged) and no wins or placed efforts from five Good-ground starts; long trip profile and hood headgear can't mask the lack of a change of gear.

runners_data.name: Sheamus Seimhiu
runners_data.note: 234 days since last run is a major red flag; natural hold-up style is compromised by the lay-off, Good ground is acceptable (3/8 sim-going), and the absence of headgear suggests connections are comfortable — but fitness must be questioned.

runners_data.name: Staywitherjohnny
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up runner with a third on Good ground over 8f and placed efforts over 9f on Soft; Shane Foley is a sharp tactical jockey who could navigate through this big field if a genuine pace develops to chase.

runners_data.name: Famous Enough
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win from this type of position on Good ground; Rory Mulligan's 5lb claim helps, 44 days since last run isn't ideal but trainer T14 1/6 suggests there's been work done, and this trip over turf suits.

runners_data.name: Real Petite
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up operator whose flagged tendency to fade makes this big competitive field tricky; 6 days since last run is quick, 135lbs, and best form has come over longer trips (16f) suggesting 1m1f could be too sharp.

runners_data.name: Virgil Tibbs
runners_data.note: 225 days off the track is a serious concern; hold-up style with a fade flag, only four visits to Good ground with no wins or places, and a 3-year-old in a field of older, more experienced handicappers — profile looks weak.

runners_data.name: Nibras Rainbow
runners_data.note: In-form prominent racer (win 13 days ago) wearing a visor; Paul Flynn's yard in strong form (T14 3/24), Good ground acceptable, though best form has come on Tapeta — the draw and big field are variables to watch.

runners_data.name: Sarmiento Power
runners_data.note: True hold-up stayer who has contested trips of 12-16f; genuinely forced into a midfield slot here because there's no room further back, and his natural finishing style is compromised — five straight figure finishes including a run 13 days ago is not encouraging.

runners_data.name: Shakita
runners_data.note: Natural rear-of-field operator from Thomas Mullins's yard whose recent form includes a long-trip background (13-16f); slotted into midfield on the map but will race further back in reality — form figures on Going and the shorter 1m1f trip both raise questions.

runners_data.name: Crypto Crash
runners_data.note: 315 days off the track after a course-marking run; a genuine long-distance hold-up type being squeezed into a midfield slot, but with no competitive form over this trip, a lengthy break and no wins on Good ground, the profile is very weak.

runners_data.name: Private Larry
runners_data.note: Three-year-old whose handful of runs are all on AW (Tapeta/Heathfield) bar one Good-ground outing; a true hold-up racer who'll want to tuck in at the rear but has been mapped to midfield — first-time turf on Good ground is a significant unknown.

runners_data.name: Desert Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 7-8f on AW for T G McCourt, wearing a hood; 90 days since last run but trainer T14 1/12 is positive — a natural hold-up type pushed toward midfield, though five seconds and thirds on a straight AW track could translate less well to Leopardstown's sweeping bend.

runners_data.name: Yquem
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer whose best efforts have come over 10f on AW; fade flag is present, Good ground is untested (4/9 sim-going) and Chris Hayes has the experience to place him well, but step to turf and a big field are negatives.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: Three-year-old apprentice-ridden (Wesley Joyce 3lb) with only four career runs; ran 3rd over 10f on Good recently at Leopardstown which is a major positive, style undetermined (U) but hood headgear and a useful weight at 121lbs make this one of the more interesting unexposed types in the race.

races.paceDynamic: Queen Aethelflaed is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no other genuine pace horse to press her, she should be able to dictate a measured, uncontested gallop from flag to finish on Good ground over 1m1f at Leopardstown. Deuteronomy, Rockbury Lad, Famous Enough and Nibras Rainbow are the principal prominent types who will likely sit in a cluster just off the leader, giving the race a conventional shape with a defined front group and a massed chasing pack. The large 17-runner field contains a surplus of hold-up and midfield horses — Private Larry, Sarmiento Power, Shakita and Crypto Crash are all genuine rear-of-field operators who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there is no room at the back for all of them, meaning their true tactical positions will be crowded and compromised. This race shape, with a lone front-runner setting a sustainable pace, most favours horses who can sit prominently and produce a clean turn of foot from the second rank — handy, well-positioned types who don't need a falsely fast pace to deliver their finishing effort.

watchPoints.text: Queen Aethelflaed is the sole pace-setter in a 17-runner field — if she gets away cleanly and Orla Tynan controls the tempo, she could steal first run and prove very hard to peg back in the straight.

The cluster of prominent types — Deuteronomy, Famous Enough, Rockbury Lad and Nibras Rainbow — will jostle for position early; any bumping or crowding at the first bend in a 17-runner field could cause interference and compromise several market principles.

Borora Aura (Wesley Joyce, 3lb) is lightly-raced and unexposed over this course and trip — its third at Leopardstown over 10f on Good is recent and potentially underrated; watch for it to be produced with a late challenge if the field spreads.

Private Larry, Sarmiento Power and Crypto Crash are all genuine long-distance or AW hold-up specialists crammed into an unfamiliar race shape — their true finishing positions will be at the rear, not midfield, and they are likely to be shuffled back as the field settles.

Sheamus Seimhiu and Virgil Tibbs both carry significant absence concerns (234 and 225 days respectively) — monitor in the parade ring for any signs of fitness, and note that both are hold-up types with fade flags who face an uphill task first time back.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Squad Builder (Q.R.) Maiden

runners_data.name: Certamen
runners_data.note: Lightly raced over staying trips on good, with trainer Buckley showing 0 from 2 in 14 days; a genuine hold-up performer who will find himself operating more forward than ideal given the volume of closers in this field, which blunts his finishing threat.

runners_data.name: Chain Of Destiny
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old returning after 18 days with a fade-in-finish flag and a mixed record on good ground; a natural hold-up horse who will be shuffled wider than suited and whose recent form string of 096/95 offers little confidence at this level.

runners_data.name: Donnrua Dream
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer with headgear (t) returning from a jumps campaign; best going evidence is sparse on good turf and Hackett's stable is 0/5 in 14 days, but the horse's natural position close to pace at least keeps it honest in this shape.

runners_data.name: Eagle Fang
runners_data.note: Long-absent (1090 days between runs before recent return), prominent racer with visor applied; placed twice at 24f on good suggests stamina is not an issue, and the step back to 1m7f from extreme trips could sharpen its finishing kick if fit enough.

runners_data.name: Joe Cool
runners_data.note: Holds solid recent form — a win at 16f on good and multiple placings — and Noel Meade's yard is operating at 2/20 in 14 days; a prominent racer who travels close to pace and whose distance profile fits this trip well.

runners_data.name: Lauro's Legend
runners_data.note: Fade-in-finish warning applies; holds one place on good ground but mostly irrelevant turf form, and a 74-day absence combined with PA Fahy's modest recent strike rate makes this hold-up type hard to place confidently.

runners_data.name: Mart Lane
runners_data.note: Prominent runner without a win in recent starts, all on soft ground; the switch to good turf at Leopardstown is an unknown variable and the 73-day absence after a modest handicap campaign raises fitness questions, though natural position close to pace keeps him involved early.

runners_data.name: Must Meet Cecil
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse with placed form on good — 0W4P — and headgear (p); Cian Collins is 2/10 in 14 days, and while Must Meet Cecil races in a more forward position than ideal, its stamina and consistency over 16f+ on good makes it a credible each-way proposition if pace develops.

runners_data.name: The Banger Doyle
runners_data.note: A decade-old campaigner with five places and no wins, returning after 308 days; by temperament a hold-up horse who will be mapped forward of his comfort zone, and the lengthy absence combined with the demanding 1m7f trip makes his task formidable.

runners_data.name: Beir Bua
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner at Leopardstown (1/18f/GOO), prominent racer with tongue tie, and Slattery's stable is striking at 4/28 in 14 days; two wins and three places in similar conditions make this the most compelling profile in the race.

runners_data.name: Faerie Tales
runners_data.note: Two-year-old with only two runs — both unplaced on good over 7-8f — stepping massively up in trip to 1m7f; a hold-up type making a huge ask at an early age and this step to extreme staying distance is almost impossible to support.

runners_data.name: Fraher Field
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on good and has multiple places over comparable trips; prominent racer whose form line of 2-11-7-1-2 includes solid Leopardstown exposure, and the Kiely yard has recent winners, making this one of the more solid claims in the field.

runners_data.name: Gaoth Chuil
runners_data.note: Has placed three times including a third over 22f on good, giving genuine staying credentials; however, the horse is a true hold-up performer who finds himself in a more forward position due to redistribution, and T M Walsh has had no recent runners, leaving fitness uncertain.

runners_data.name: Golden Fascination
runners_data.note: Lightly raced, no historical form provided, going marked UNKNOWN — an entirely opaque proposition; Cian Collins has been active (2/14 in 14 days) but without past performance data this runner must be treated as an unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Kaleo Ametsa
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with consistent mid-table finishes on good (0W, sim-going 4/7), tongue tie applied; Josh Halley's yard is 0/4 in 14 days and the horse's best efforts over 16-20f suggest stamina is there, but the style mismatch versus available positions caps expectations.

runners_data.name: Kimy
runners_data.note: Thomas Mullins is 1/5 in 14 days and Kimy has a win over 16f on good; a hold-up horse with headgear (p) and placed form on good ground who, while out of natural position, has enough class and trip suitability to pick up pieces if something goes wrong upfront.

runners_data.name: Salsinha
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner, with two wins and four places over 16f on good/soft; Henry De Bromhead is firing at 11/39 in 14 days, and the horse carries a STYLE_FIT note suggesting the prominent tag slightly undersells a horse that genuinely wants to lead — this is its race to set up.

runners_data.name: Wonderwalk
runners_data.note: Three-year-old stepping up to 1m7f after a 340-day absence; wears hood and has finished placed at 18f on good, but a hold-up type bumped forward by redistribution, combined with extreme youth and a long layoff, means it faces serious challenges in this competitive field.

races.paceDynamic: Salsinha is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner maiden over 1m7f at Leopardstown, and with no genuine rival to push for the lead, she is positioned to dictate a controlled, measured gallop on good ground — a classic lone-leader scenario where the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. Beir Bua, Joe Cool, Fraher Field, Donnrua Dream, Eagle Fang, and Mart Lane are all genuine prominent types who will fan out behind her in the early stages, creating a competitive mid-race order but not a gruelling early burn-out. This field contains more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Certamen, The Banger Doyle, Gaoth Chuil, and Wonderwalk are true closers who will be shuffled into midfield rather than their natural position, meaning they race partially out of role. With a sole front-runner setting a sustainable tempo in a large field, the race shape strongly favours prominent racers who travel close to the pace and can sustain their effort over the final two furlongs rather than those relying on a strong late injection.

watchPoints.text: Beir Bua has won twice over course and distance on good ground and races prominently — if Salsinha is allowed to find a comfortable rhythm, Beir Bua tracking in second or third is perfectly positioned to pounce in the straight.

Salsinha as sole front-runner holds an unusually powerful tactical lever in an 18-runner field — watch whether she is allowed to bowl along uncontested, as any increase in early pace from the chasing pack behind her changes the entire race shape dramatically.

Joe Cool and Fraher Field both carry recent placed form on good ground and are natural prominent racers — if either lands a prominent pitch directly behind Salsinha, they become serious threats to dominate the final two furlongs.

The block of redistributed hold-up horses — Certamen, The Banger Doyle, Gaoth Chuil — will be operating forward of their natural position; if they unsettle one another in the early stages or take a prominent role that doesn't suit, it could create mid-race congestion and influence the finish.

Golden Fascination is entirely unquantified — unknown going preference, no public form — and with Cian Collins booked and the yard in form, an unheralded debut run cannot be entirely dismissed if it shows natural ability in the early stages.
